stem: During routine care of a client's PICC, the nurse notes new tenderness at the insertion site and a transparent dressing that has become damp and loosened. What is the best action?

options.A: Inspect the site for local infection or other complication and replace the compromised dressing using aseptic technique
options.B: Leave the dressing in place until the next scheduled change because PICC dressings should not be changed early
options.C: Cover the loose dressing with additional tape without inspecting the insertion site
options.D: Ignore the tenderness if the client is afebrile because local findings do not suggest catheter-related infection

rationale: CDC intravascular-catheter guidance recommends regular visual/palpation assessment of catheter sites. If tenderness or other findings suggest local or bloodstream infection, the site should be thoroughly examined. Catheter dressings should be replaced when damp, loosened, or visibly soiled, and catheter care should use aseptic technique. A compromised dressing should not simply be taped over or left until a routine date. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Recognize PICC-site tenderness and a damp/loose dressing as findings requiring site assessment and aseptic dressing replacement rather than waiting for the routine change interval.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Background Information: Strategies for Prevention of Catheter-Related Infections; Basic Infection Control and Prevention Plan for Outpatient Oncology Settings
source_version_date: Current CDC catheter guidance pages accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Catheter Site Dressing Regimens: replace dressing if damp, loosened, or visibly soiled; monitor sites visually/palpation and remove dressing for thorough examination when tenderness or infection manifestations are present. Outpatient Oncology > Changing Catheter Site Dressing: applies to PICCs; maintain aseptic technique, remove dressing and inspect site visually
source_claim_supported: PICC sites require ongoing assessment; tenderness prompts examination and a damp/loose dressing should be replaced using aseptic technique.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — invasive-device infection prevention, aseptic technique, and recognition of infection-control breaches
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — PICC site assessment and dressing care
correction_summary: Removed the source item's peripheral-IV-oriented 'infection, phlebitis, or infiltration' cluster and rebuilt it around CDC central-catheter/PICC site-care findings: tenderness, inspection, compromised dressing, and aseptic replacement.
audit_findings: A matches CDC. B ignores the condition-based dressing-change rule; C fails to inspect and restore an intact sterile dressing; D falsely dismisses a local warning sign in the absence of fever. No unnecessary scheduled-frequency precision or second answer remains. Independent adversarial second pass passed.
